gaps.sentence: 'I can't find my passport anywhere,' she moaned. She moaned that she ___ find her passport anywhere.
gaps.explanation: Negative can backshifts to couldn't in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Please reconsider my application,' she wrote. She ___ them to reconsider her application.
gaps.explanation: A polite written request is reported with asked + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
gaps.explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
gaps.explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.
